title: Progressive Deploy Visual Language & Quickstart Screens
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design and produce a compact, platform-consistent visual language and quickstart screens for Redwood Console that teach users how to create progressive deployments: canary, A/B experiment, and multi-stage fallback policies. This ticket covers illustration assets, annotated screenshots, and a short sequence of hero frames for the quickstart flow used in the onboarding modal and docs.
goals: Provide an at-a-glance visual metaphor for version pinning and fallback chains
Create assets that scale from small quickstart cards to full-width docs banners
deliverables: 8 vector icons representing variant states and traffic split
Figma file with componentized policy editor mockups
Exported PNG/SVG assets for docs and Console
screenshots_needed: Policy editor with canary traffic slider and tooltip
A/B split preview with performance preview cards
Fallback chain editor expanded showing chained targets and health thresholds
Empty state when no pinned versions exist with CTA
tasks: Finalize icon set and tokenized colors
Produce annotated screenshots for docs page
Prepare 3 hero frames sized for modal (640x320) and docs banner (1200x360)
Stage assets in Drive and link to PR for docs update
accept_criteria: All assets assembled in Figma and exported to Drive
Docs PR references exported assets and includes screenshots
Design review sign-off from PM (Ava Patel) and Eng lead (Ravi Singh)
Accessible color contrast validated for icons and overlays
comments: 2025-02-11 Maya Chen: Initial exploratory sketches posted to Figma. Chose traffic-funnel metaphor over server-stack imagery per PM feedback.
2025-02-18 Liam O'Connor: Iterated hero frames — reduced copy length and introduced numbered microsteps. Uploaded v2 hero PNGs to Drive.
2025-02-24 Ravi Singh: Engineering review: please ensure policy editor mockups map to current API fields (we need 'health_threshold' and 'failover_timeout' visible). Marked ENG-5125 as dependency.
2025-02-28 Ava Patel: Suggested adding a compact keyboard-navigable variant picker for accessibility — flagged as stretch but high priority for docs.
2025-03-03 Sofia Lopez: Design review complete. Requested updated annotation callouts and microcopy tweaks for the canary tooltip. Assigned final polish to Liam.
2025-03-04 Liam O'Connor: Uploaded final exports (v3). Drafted PR to update docs: GH-PR #8742. Leaving in-review for PM/Eng signoff.
decisions: Use traffic-funnel visual metaphor for hero frames (more intuitive for PM/UX tests)
Prioritize compact modal-first layout for quickstart; full-width pages use expanded variants
Icons must be mono-line with a single filled accent matching Redwood token 'redwood-700' for active state
review_feedback: PM: shorten hero header copy to one line
Eng: expose API field names in advanced view mockups
Docs: include alt text drafts for each screenshot
next_steps: Resolve microcopy for canary tooltip (assigned to Maya)
Merge docs PR after PM signoff
Add exported assets to CDN and update relative paths in docs page
notes_on_tradeoffs: Chose simpler funnel imagery over literal server diagrams to lower cognitive load for non-ops users
Compact modal sacrifices some advanced field visibility; added 'Advanced' toggle to surface extra fields instead
qa_checklist: Verify exported PNGs are within 2x asset sizes for retina
Run color contrast tests on all overlays
Confirm mobile modal layout on iOS and Android emulators
ux_research_plan: A/B test two hero frame sequences with new signups (canary-first vs A/B-first)
Track time-to-pin and completion rate in onboarding funnel for 2 weeks after release
customer_notes: Include brief why/when guidance: 'Use canary for incremental traffic verification; use A/B for experiments; use fallback to stay online if newer versions fail'
